variants.direction: Make the fuselage sides into a decisive shallow wedge: a high solid shoulder immediately behind the collars, one diagonal lower edge rising toward the stern, and a deep broad trapezoidal side recess following that slope. The cargo roof remains nearly level. Expose a short solid saddle below each flank for the compact forward fan pivot. Fan leaves have long straight diagonal outer ends with neatly clipped corners. Use a straight wide spoiler with short downturned tips and simple sloping supports. Give both engines separate octagonal cuffs. variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Draw ONE new industrial game-concept sheet for the pirate Liberty elite fighter from Freelancer. Continue the promising L08/L09 direction while making the specific structural variation below clearly visible. Simple geometric components assembled into a rich functional ship, medium detail, recognizable Liberty family. This is a fighter of the original scale, with full hull height and a deployed span close to its length.

ORDERED INPUT IMAGES:
1 = authoritative ORIGINAL COCKPIT. Preserve its complete elongated rounded capsule shell, original size, thin window frames, large curved blue-grey side panes, long top pane and little rear quarter panes. The glazed cabin itself is the nose. Copy its contour rather than redesigning it; no extra nose beak or thick window armor. Preserve three thin transverse neck collars behind it. This reference overrides any cockpit drift in concepts 2/3.
2 = L08 visual direction, useful shape, detail density and sheet presentation.
3 = L09 visual direction, useful flank cut and separate stern components. These two are direction references, not drawings to duplicate.
4 = ACTUAL three-leaf folding motion. Each side has THREE BROAD OVERLAPPING RIGID LEAVES forming ONE FAN. The compact chain of pivots is concentrated near the FRONT root of the main hull, immediately behind the neck collars. Each whole leaf extends beneath its neighbor; leaves radiate sideways and backward from that root. For docking, same-size leaves rotate backward and overlap close along the hull. No three independent fingers hinged at three distant stations along the body, no telescoping or shrinking leaves. Show the correct continuous broad fan area.
5 = ACTUAL source component assembly. Retain a separate raised transverse rear SPOILER with downturned ends and visible air below, two individually readable vertically stacked rear engines, shaped central body and roof baydoor. Upper engine is wider/shorter, lower engine narrower/longer and farther aft. Colors in refs 4/5 explain parts only, not desired paint.

INVARIANTS: unchanged original cabin and neck collars; compact articulated front wing roots; exactly three solid overlapping leaves per side; one separate transverse spoiler; two distinct unequal engines on a VERTICAL CENTERLINE, not side by side; full body height. Two narrow long cargo roof doors sit side by side, hinge along outer long edges, seam running NOSE TO TAIL; clear opening/sweep, spoiler behind the doors. Keep connected solid mounts and purposeful transitions. Preserve negative spaces under spoiler and around engine attachments.

DESIGN LANGUAGE: angular hull sections, strong plane changes, a few purposeful recesses and functional medium-size housings. Calm large surfaces, sparse service seams and repaired replacement plates. Pirate alteration is built into shape and mechanical connections. No exposed pipes, rod scaffolding, ornamental framing, cathedral towers, stacked decorative ribs, tiny rivets, skulls or spikes. Use the same restrained steel/off-white/oxide-red palette throughout this series so shape differences lead.

Small TOP STOWED inset showing those same three leaves nested backward along the body. No shrinking body or changing cockpit between views. Text only the variant code plus SIDE, TOP, REAR, STOWED.

variants.direction: Focus this variant on three especially broad overlapping angular fan leaves with clipped chisel-shaped tips, forming a full stepped fan almost as wide as the ship is long. This is a broad expressive fan around a lean, deep body, not a flattened aircraft.
